messages:
support-jen: Heads up — ACME reported a big p99 regression on embeddings API starting ~02:15 UTC yesterday. They attached logs showing p95 ~180ms -> 420ms and p99 jumps to ~950ms. They're seeing timeouts in a few requests.

maria-oncall: Thanks, Jen. Any correlation with infra changes?

support-jen: Customer says they didn't change anything. Our deploy history shows a host kernel and CUDA driver rollout that finished around 02:10 UTC in eu-west-1.

alex-runtime: Pinging infra for correlation. I quickly checked RB metrics: model-serving p99 for the embeddings route spiked exactly at 02:12 UTC across multiple nodes. Request CPU on the host jumped and host io wait went from 3% -> 26%.

luke-infra: I'm seeing the same on the node pool. NVMe IOPS look normal but avg read latency on some devices spiked to 20-40ms. Suspect IO contention after the driver update.

jordan-ml: Could KV cache be falling back to disk? Cache miss rate increased at the same time. If big models lose cached KV pages we do a lot more host reads.

alex-runtime: Repro steps I'm running locally: curl embeddings call (100 reqs), capture per-token latency. With cache warm: p99 ~140ms. After forcing kv cache flush: p99 ~980ms and I see lots of `nvme` read stalls in dstat.

maria-oncall: Can you paste the quick logs/commands here?

alex-runtime: Sure — commands I ran:

```bash
# warm cache workload
for i in {1..100}; do curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.test/embeddings" -d '@payload.json' & done
# flush kv cache (dev only) and rerun
kill -USR1 $(pgrep redis-like-kv)
# quick NVMe check
iostat -x 1 5
nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1
```

Alex's iostat excerpt:
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s r_await w_await aqu-sz  %util
nvme0n1         1200.0   50.0  48000.0  1024.0    0.00   0.00   18.50   0.22   1.30  98.1
```

luke-infra: dmesg on one of the impacted hosts shows periodic timeouts: `nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 2 timeout, resetting controller`. Also some GPU driver messages: `NVRM: GPU ID ... reset` but not full device loss.

sre-bot: Incident tag assigned: INCIDENT-2026-042. Pager duty notified.

maria-oncall: Immediate mitigation options? Can we divert traffic or enable fallback model to avoid p99s for customers while we triage?

alex-runtime: We can switch routing for embeddings route to dedicated pool that didn't receive the driver update (eu-west-1b) and enable burst cap to soak traffic. Also we can switch customers to a smaller embedding model variant with lower KV pressure.

luke-infra: I'm going to cordon the most affected nodes and roll them back to the previous NVMe firmware/driver on a canary to test. Rolling back a kernel/driver statewide is risky.

jordan-ml: I'll prepare a rollback plan for the runtime that pins the model bundle to avoid cache invalidation during the node-level rollbacks. Also will add more aggressive prefetch config on canary to prove if cache behavior helps.

support-jen: I told the customer we've enabled fallback routing and are investigating root cause; offered temporary rate limits and prioritized their traffic to the unaffected pool. They accepted.

luke-infra: Quick summary of initial findings:
- spike coincides with CUDA/driver + host kernel rollout at 02:10 UTC
- affected nodes: 6/24 in the eu-west-1 serving pool (mixed HW)
- symptoms: NVMe I/O latency spikes, intermittent controller resets, increased host io wait -> KV cache misses -> more host reads -> compounding latency
- some GPU reset messages but no core GPU crash seen

alex-runtime: We did a quick canary rollback on one node: reverted the driver to previous package, restarted runtime, warmed KV cache. Result: p99 returned to ~150ms for that node's traffic within 6 minutes.

maria-oncall: Good. What's the riskiest next step?

luke-infra: Scaling-wise the safe path: cordon + roll back in small batches, validate cache warm and tail latency. If node-level rollback fixes consistently, we can schedule wider rollback. The risky path is keeping current stack and trying kernel knobs to mask symptoms (e.g., changing elevator, io_scheduler), which might hide root cause and delay rollback.

jordan-ml: Also filing a follow-up to analyze KV eviction policy — if driver changes change IO latency distribution, we may want a more tolerant eviction threshold to avoid sudden disk fallbacks.

alex-runtime: For short-term: changed routing, cordoned 3 worst nodes, rolled back 1 as test, prepared canary verification script:

```bash
# canary verification
#!/bin/bash
for i in {1..200}; do 
  start=$(date +%s%3N)
  curl -s -X POST "https://canary.redwood.local/embeddings" -d @payload.json > /dev/null
  end=$(date +%s%3N)
  echo $((end-start)) >> latencies.txt
done
python3 - <<'PY'
import numpy as np
xs = list(map(int, open('latencies.txt')))
print('p95', np.percentile(xs,95), 'p99', np.percentile(xs,99))
PY
```

maria-oncall: Timeline update for the customer and execs?

support-jen: Sent a note 30m ago: we have mitigations in place (traffic reroute + limited rollback work), canary rollback shows positive results, next update in 60m.

luke-infra: Next actions (short):
- continue rolling back drivers in small batches (infra team)
- run full NVMe health checks on all affected hosts (nvme-cli, smart logs)
- add telemetry to correlate KV miss -> host read bytes -> nvme latency
- prepare postmortem template: change event, impact, mitigations, test plan to avoid reintroducing bad driver bundle

jordan-ml: Long term: evaluate cache eviction thresholds and add an early-warning metric for when host io read amplification > X MB/s for embedding routes.

alex-runtime: I'll also add a temporary runtime knob to reduce KV cache memory pressure for heavy embedding workloads until we stabilize drivers.

maria-oncall: Ok. If p99 stays under control for the next 2 hours on the customer region, we'll de-escalate. Keep me posted.

support-jen: Customer replied: "Thanks — we see improvement. Please keep us updated." :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, impacted_customers=[ACME Corp], owner=luke-infra.

maria-oncall: Closing loop: collect all node-level artifacts (dmesg, nvme smart-log, iostat, runtime logs, kv cache metrics) and upload to INCIDENT-2026-042. I'll own the postmortem draft.

luke-infra: Uploading canary artifacts now. Will follow up with a proposed rollback window for the remaining affected nodes.

alex-runtime: Noted. I'll add the canary verification results to the incident.

support-jen: Thanks everyone.
